Prevention: Lablab ( Lablab purpureus ) or cowpea for intercropping and/or cover crops to prevent weed establishment and spread
Seeds can travel on animals, do not allow animals into an affected area
Avoid heavy grazing and browsing since the weed thrives in open, disturbed areas
Clean tools and farm machinery to prevent seeds being spread
Control adventive individual plants in the vicinity by digging out the roots to prevent spread
Remove plants before they set seed, as seeds dispersed by wind and water are difficult to manage
Clean shoes, clothing and hair after being in an infested area.
Use certified clean seed for growing crops; seeds considered as the main means of spread
Consider applying pre- ermergence herbicide (refer to yellow list) if infestation is present
Monitoring: Evergreen shrub that may climb up trees (2–7 m high), often forming dense thickets.
Stems yellowish- green and somewhat hairy; deep taproot.
Leaves light green, hairy, triangular (5–12 cm long and 3–7 cm wide), three conspicuous veins from the base; smell strongly of turpentine when crushed.
Flowers pale purple, in cylindrical heads at the ends of stems.
Seeds straw- coloured, (4–5 mm long) with long bristles.

Regularly surveillance of tracks, grazing places, previously flooded areas and areas where machinery and equipment is stored for seedling establishment - two weekly in the rainy season and monthly in the dry season
Check for flowering plants and seed formation and take action of direct control to prevent seed set and establishment of a seed bank
Regularly monitor fields, fallow land and surrounding areas for presence of the weed and take action of direct control if found
Direct Control: Dig out root system by hand or using machinery 10-15 cm below the soil surface to remove growing point– this will be easier if soil is wet.
Repeat twice during the growing season
Slashing or cutting is not effective as weed will coppice profusely from the roots
Hand-pull seedlings and young plants including the whole root system.
Repeat every 2-3 months afterwards due to rapid regrowth
Do not leave root fragments on ground as they can take root and grow
Consider using biological control such as the
Chromolaena stem gall fly ( Cecidochares connexa )
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
C. odorata is most susceptible to chemical control when it is growing vigorously, such as at the beginning of the rainy season.
Best control using a foliar herbicide is usually obtained when herbicides are applied to young shoots after slashing.
Application of herbicides to cut-stump also effective

Use triclopyr as cut stump treatments when clearing the land; it is important to apply chemical to the cut stump within 1 minute; triclopyr (480g/l) as 100ml pre 10 l of diesel, cut the stumps 10 cm above ground and apply to all exposed surfaces of the plant; Triclopyr
Spray foliar herbicides (glyphosate, triclopyr, metsulfuron- methyl) when plant is actively growing and to young re-growth after slashing
U (unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use)
